_note: Editorial demo catalogue. Practical facts (hours, fees) are null unless widely documented, and every destination starts with factsVerified=false. Admins verify facts and add sources from the Admin dashboard. Coordinates and images are refined from Wikipedia at startup.

destinations.name: Taj Mahal
destinations.summary: Shah Jahan's white-marble mausoleum on the Yamuna — India's most recognisable monument and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
destinations.summaryHi: यमुना किनारे शाहजहाँ द्वारा बनवाया गया सफ़ेद संगमरमर का मक़बरा — यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर स्थल।
destinations.description: The Taj Mahal is an ivory-white marble mausoleum set within a formal Mughal garden (charbagh) on the south bank of the Yamuna in Agra. Its symmetry, calligraphy and pietra dura inlay make it the finest example of Mughal architecture.
destinations.history: Mughal emperor Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal in 1632 as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died in 1631. The main mausoleum was completed around 1643 and the wider complex around 1653, built by thousands of artisans; the design is commonly attributed to Ustad Ahmad Lahauri. Shah Jahan himself was later buried beside Mumtaz Mahal. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
destinations.culturalSignificance: Widely regarded as a symbol of love and as the jewel of Indo-Islamic architecture, the Taj Mahal blends Persian, Timurid and Indian design traditions and is among the most visited monuments in the world.
destinations.openingHours: Sunrise to sunset; closed on Fridays
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March (cooler months). Early morning offers softer light and smaller crowds.
destinations.guidelines: Security screening at entry gates; carry minimal baggage. Respect the mausoleum's silence and do not touch the inlay work.

destinations.name: Agra Fort
destinations.summary: A vast red-sandstone Mughal fort-palace whose marble pavilions look across the Yamuna to the Taj Mahal.
destinations.summaryHi: लाल बलुआ पत्थर का विशाल मुग़ल किला, जहाँ से यमुना पार ताज महल दिखाई देता है।
destinations.description: Agra Fort is a walled city of palaces, audience halls and mosques enclosed by massive red-sandstone ramparts. Highlights include the Diwan-i-Am, Diwan-i-Khas, Jahangiri Mahal and the octagonal Musamman Burj.
destinations.history: Emperor Akbar rebuilt the fort in red sandstone from 1565. His grandson Shah Jahan added refined white-marble palaces and mosques. After Aurangzeb seized power in 1658, Shah Jahan spent his final years confined here, traditionally said to have gazed at the Taj Mahal from the Musamman Burj. The fort became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
destinations.culturalSignificance: The fort charts the evolution of Mughal architecture across three generations of emperors and was the seat of Mughal power for much of the 16th and 17th centuries.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March. Combine with the Taj Mahal on the same day.
destinations.guidelines: Large parts are open-air; carry water and sun protection. Some areas are closed to visitors.

destinations.name: Fatehpur Sikri
destinations.summary: Akbar's short-lived red-sandstone capital, about 40 km from Agra, with the towering Buland Darwaza.
destinations.summaryHi: आगरा से लगभग 40 किमी दूर अकबर की लाल पत्थर की राजधानी, जहाँ भव्य बुलंद दरवाज़ा है।
destinations.description: Fatehpur Sikri is a remarkably preserved Mughal city of palaces, courtyards and a great mosque. Visitors explore the royal complex (Panch Mahal, Diwan-i-Khas) and the Jama Masjid with the shrine of Sufi saint Salim Chishti and the monumental Buland Darwaza.
destinations.history: Emperor Akbar founded Fatehpur Sikri around 1571 to honour the Sufi saint Shaikh Salim Chishti, whose blessing he credited for the birth of his heir. It served as the Mughal capital for roughly 14 years before being largely abandoned; water scarcity and political needs are commonly cited reasons. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.
destinations.culturalSignificance: The city reflects Akbar's syncretic vision, blending Hindu, Persian and Islamic architectural vocabularies. The dargah of Salim Chishti remains an active place of pilgrimage for people of many faiths.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March; start early to avoid midday heat.
destinations.guidelines: The mosque and dargah are active places of worship — dress modestly and remove footwear where required.

destinations.name: Itmad-ud-Daulah's Tomb
destinations.summary: The 'Baby Taj' — an exquisite marble tomb with pioneering pietra dura inlay on the Yamuna's east bank.
destinations.summaryHi: 'बेबी ताज' — यमुना के पूर्वी तट पर बारीक पच्चीकारी वाला सुंदर संगमरमर मक़बरा।
destinations.description: A jewel-box mausoleum set in a riverside garden, faced in white marble and covered with intricate inlaid stone, latticework and painted interiors.
destinations.history: Empress Nur Jahan built the tomb between about 1622 and 1628 for her father, Mirza Ghiyas Beg, who held the title I'timād-ud-Daulah ('pillar of the state'). It is often described as the first Mughal tomb faced in white marble with extensive pietra dura, foreshadowing the Taj Mahal.
destinations.culturalSignificance: It marks a turning point from red sandstone to white marble in Mughal architecture and showcases the influence of Nur Jahan as a patron of the arts.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March; late afternoon light suits the marble.

destinations.name: Mehtab Bagh
destinations.summary: A Mughal riverside garden directly across the Yamuna from the Taj Mahal — a calm spot for sunset views.
destinations.summaryHi: यमुना पार ताज महल के ठीक सामने मुग़ल बाग़ — सूर्यास्त के नज़ारों के लिए शांत जगह।
destinations.description: Mehtab Bagh ('moonlight garden') is a charbagh-style garden aligned with the Taj Mahal on the opposite bank of the Yamuna, offering an unobstructed view of the monument.
destinations.history: The garden is traditionally associated with the chain of Mughal gardens laid out along the Yamuna, and its alignment with the Taj Mahal has led historians to see it as part of the Taj complex's wider design. It was restored after archaeological work in the 1990s.
destinations.culturalSignificance: A favourite viewpoint for photographers and a reminder of Agra's historic riverfront garden landscape.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: Around sunset, October to March.

destinations.name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
destinations.summary: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Shiva and the spiritual heart of Varanasi.
destinations.summaryHi: शिव के बारह ज्योतिर्लिंगों में से एक और वाराणसी का आध्यात्मिक केंद्र।
destinations.description: The Kashi Vishwanath Temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva as Vishwanatha ('Lord of the Universe'), stands near the western bank of the Ganga. The Kashi Vishwanath Corridor now links the temple directly to the riverfront ghats.
destinations.history: A temple to Vishwanatha has stood in Kashi for many centuries and was destroyed and rebuilt several times. The present temple was built in 1780 by Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore; Maharaja Ranjit Singh later donated gold to plate its spires. The Kashi Vishwanath Dham corridor was inaugurated in December 2021.
destinations.culturalSignificance: Varanasi is among the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, and a visit to Vishwanatha is considered one of the holiest acts in Hinduism. The temple is central to festivals such as Maha Shivaratri.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March. Expect very large crowds on Mondays, Shivaratri and in the month of Shravan.
destinations.guidelines: Strict security: rules on phones, bags and items allowed inside can change — check the official temple website before visiting. Dress modestly.

destinations.name: Dashashwamedh Ghat
destinations.summary: Varanasi's busiest ghat, famous for the nightly Ganga Aarti with lamps, conches and chants.
destinations.summaryHi: वाराणसी का सबसे व्यस्त घाट, जहाँ हर शाम भव्य गंगा आरती होती है।
destinations.description: Dashashwamedh is the main ghat on the Ganga close to Kashi Vishwanath. Each evening priests perform the Ganga Aarti, a choreographed ritual of fire, incense and music watched from the steps and from boats.
destinations.history: According to legend, Lord Brahma performed the dasha-ashwamedha (ten-horse) sacrifice here, giving the ghat its name. The stone ghat was rebuilt in the 18th century under Maratha patronage.
destinations.culturalSignificance: The evening Ganga Aarti has become one of the defining experiences of Varanasi for pilgrims and travellers alike.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: Evenings, October to March. Arrive early for a spot on the steps or book a boat.
destinations.guidelines: Very crowded at aarti time — keep valuables secure. Agree boat fares before boarding.

destinations.name: Sarnath
destinations.summary: Where the Buddha gave his first sermon — home to the Dhamek Stupa and Ashoka's Lion Capital.
destinations.summaryHi: जहाँ बुद्ध ने अपना पहला उपदेश दिया — धमेख स्तूप और अशोक का सिंह स्तंभ शीर्ष यहीं है।
destinations.description: Sarnath, about 10 km north-east of central Varanasi, is a serene complex of stupas, monastery ruins, temples built by Buddhist communities from many countries, and an archaeological museum.
destinations.history: After his enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, the Buddha delivered his first sermon, setting the Wheel of Dharma in motion, at the deer park of Sarnath. Emperor Ashoka erected stupas and a pillar here in the 3rd century BCE; the Lion Capital from that pillar was adopted as the National Emblem of India and is displayed in the Sarnath Museum.
destinations.culturalSignificance: Sarnath is one of the four principal Buddhist pilgrimage sites and a symbol of India's national identity through the Ashokan emblem.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March. Combine with a morning on the ghats.
destinations.guidelines: Maintain silence near shrines and meditating pilgrims. The museum is typically closed one day a week — check before going.

destinations.name: Assi Ghat
destinations.summary: The southernmost major ghat — known for its sunrise ceremony, cafés and relaxed riverside atmosphere.
destinations.summaryHi: दक्षिणी छोर का प्रमुख घाट — सुबह की आरती, कैफ़े और शांत माहौल के लिए प्रसिद्ध।
destinations.description: Assi Ghat sits where the Assi stream meets the Ganga. Mornings bring yoga, music and an aarti; the surrounding lanes are full of cafés, bookshops and guesthouses popular with students and travellers.
destinations.history: The ghat is mentioned in Hindu texts as a place of pilgrimage, and the poet-saint Tulsidas is traditionally associated with the nearby area where he composed parts of the Ramcharitmanas.
destinations.culturalSignificance: A starting point for boat rides along the ghats and a hub of Varanasi's contemporary cultural life.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: Sunrise, October to March.

destinations.name: Ramnagar Fort
destinations.summary: The 18th-century riverside fort of the Maharajas of Benares, with a museum of royal collections.
destinations.summaryHi: बनारस के महाराजाओं का 18वीं सदी का गंगा किनारे बना किला, जिसमें शाही संग्रहालय है।
destinations.description: Built in cream-coloured sandstone on the east bank of the Ganga opposite the main ghats, Ramnagar Fort houses a museum with vintage cars, palanquins, weapons and costumes of the Kashi royal family.
destinations.history: The fort was built in the mid-18th century by Raja Balwant Singh, the ruler of Benares, and remains the ancestral residence of the Kashi Naresh (Maharaja of Benares).
destinations.culturalSignificance: Ramnagar is famous for its month-long Ramlila, a centuries-old open-air enactment of the Ramayana staged across the town under royal patronage.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March; the Ramlila takes place around Dussehra.

destinations.name: Bara Imambara
destinations.summary: Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula's grand imambara, famous for its vast vaulted hall and the Bhool Bhulaiya labyrinth.
destinations.summaryHi: नवाब आसफ़-उद-दौला का भव्य इमामबाड़ा, विशाल हॉल और भूल-भुलैया के लिए प्रसिद्ध।
destinations.description: The Bara Imambara complex includes the main hall, the Asfi Mosque and a stepwell (baoli). Above the hall lies the Bhool Bhulaiya, a maze of narrow passages and balconies.
destinations.history: Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula built the Bara Imambara in 1784, partly as a famine-relief project that provided employment during a severe drought. Its central hall is celebrated as one of the largest arched halls built without supporting beams.
destinations.culturalSignificance: An imambara is a congregation hall for Shia commemorations, especially during Muharram. The complex is the most iconic monument of Nawabi Lucknow.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March.
destinations.guidelines: A religious site — dress modestly. Hiring a registered guide is recommended for the Bhool Bhulaiya.

destinations.name: Rumi Darwaza
destinations.summary: A soaring 18th-century Awadhi gateway that has become the emblem of Lucknow.
destinations.summaryHi: 18वीं सदी का भव्य अवधी द्वार, जो लखनऊ की पहचान बन गया है।
destinations.description: The Rumi Darwaza is an ornate ceremonial gateway about 18 metres tall, standing between the Bara Imambara and the Chota Imambara in old Lucknow.
destinations.history: It was built in 1784 under Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula alongside the Bara Imambara. It is often called the 'Turkish Gate' because of a perceived resemblance to an Ottoman gateway in Istanbul.
destinations.culturalSignificance: The gate is the most recognised symbol of Lucknow and of Awadhi architecture.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: Evening, when the gate is lit; October to March.

destinations.name: Chota Imambara
destinations.summary: The Hussainabad Imambara — a 19th-century hall famous for its chandeliers and gilded dome.
destinations.summaryHi: हुसैनाबाद इमामबाड़ा — झूमरों और सुनहरे गुंबद के लिए प्रसिद्ध 19वीं सदी की इमारत।
destinations.description: Also called the Imambara Hussainabad Mubarak, it is decorated with chandeliers, calligraphy and a gilded dome, and contains the tombs of its builder and his family.
destinations.history: Nawab Muhammad Ali Shah built the Chota Imambara in 1838 as a congregation hall for Shia Muslims and as his own mausoleum.
destinations.culturalSignificance: It is beautifully illuminated during Muharram and other festivals and is a key part of the Hussainabad heritage zone.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March.

destinations.name: The Residency, Lucknow
destinations.summary: Shell-scarred ruins of the British Residency, preserved as a memorial to the 1857 Siege of Lucknow.
destinations.summaryHi: 1857 की लखनऊ घेराबंदी की याद में संरक्षित ब्रिटिश रेज़िडेंसी के खंडहर।
destinations.description: Set in landscaped gardens, the Residency complex comprises ruined buildings still marked by cannon fire, a cemetery and a small museum describing the events of 1857.
destinations.history: The complex was built in the late 18th century as the residence of the British Resident at the court of the Nawabs of Awadh. During the uprising of 1857 it was besieged for months, and the ruins have been preserved largely as they were left.
destinations.culturalSignificance: A significant site for understanding the 1857 uprising, remembered in India as the First War of Independence.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March; mornings are pleasant for walking the grounds.

destinations.name: Ambedkar Memorial Park
destinations.summary: A vast red-sandstone memorial park in Gomti Nagar honouring Dr B. R. Ambedkar and social reformers.
destinations.summaryHi: गोमती नगर में डॉ. बी. आर. आंबेडकर और समाज सुधारकों को समर्पित विशाल स्मारक पार्क।
destinations.description: The park features monumental red-sandstone structures, statues, a stupa-like memorial and broad plazas, and is popular for evening walks.
destinations.history: The memorial was developed by the Uttar Pradesh government in the 2000s and opened in 2008, dedicated to Dr B. R. Ambedkar and other leaders of social justice movements.
destinations.culturalSignificance: An important site of remembrance for the legacy of Dr Ambedkar and the movement against caste discrimination.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: Evenings, October to March.

destinations.name: Ram Mandir, Ayodhya
destinations.summary: The grand Nagara-style temple at the site revered as the birthplace of Lord Rama.
destinations.summaryHi: भगवान राम की जन्मभूमि मानी जाने वाली जगह पर बना भव्य नागर शैली का मंदिर।
destinations.description: The Ram Mandir is a large stone temple built in the North Indian Nagara style at the Ram Janmabhoomi site in Ayodhya, a major pilgrimage destination on the banks of the Sarayu.
destinations.history: Construction began after the Supreme Court of India's 2019 verdict on the Ayodhya dispute. The consecration ceremony (pran pratishtha) of the idol of Ram Lalla was held on 22 January 2024, while further construction of the complex continued afterwards.
destinations.culturalSignificance: Ayodhya is one of Hinduism's seven sacred cities (Saptapuri), and the temple is a focal point of devotion for millions of pilgrims.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March. Expect heavy crowds during Ram Navami and Diwali (Deepotsav).
destinations.guidelines: Strict security and restrictions on items such as phones and bags may apply — check current rules before you go. Dress modestly.

destinations.name: Hanuman Garhi
destinations.summary: A hilltop fort-like temple to Lord Hanuman, traditionally visited before other shrines in Ayodhya.
destinations.summaryHi: भगवान हनुमान का किले जैसा पहाड़ी मंदिर, जहाँ अयोध्या के अन्य मंदिरों से पहले दर्शन की परंपरा है।
destinations.description: Reached by a flight of steps, Hanuman Garhi is one of Ayodhya's most visited temples, with views over the old town.
destinations.history: The temple-fort is generally dated to the 18th century and is associated with the Nawabs of Awadh, who are said to have granted land for its construction.
destinations.culturalSignificance: By tradition, pilgrims seek Hanuman's blessing here before visiting the Ram temple, reflecting Hanuman's role as Rama's devoted protector.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: Early morning, October to March; Tuesdays and Saturdays are busiest.
destinations.guidelines: Watch belongings around monkeys. Dress modestly and remove footwear before entering.

destinations.name: Triveni Sangam
destinations.summary: The sacred confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and the mythical Saraswati — site of the Kumbh Mela.
destinations.summaryHi: गंगा, यमुना और पौराणिक सरस्वती का पवित्र संगम — कुंभ मेले का स्थल।
destinations.description: Boats take visitors from the riverbank to the meeting point of the muddy Ganga and the greener Yamuna, where pilgrims take a ritual dip.
destinations.history: The Sangam has been a place of pilgrimage for millennia and is the venue of the Kumbh Mela, one of the largest religious gatherings on Earth, held here in a cycle of years; the Maha Kumbh took place in 2025.
destinations.culturalSignificance: Bathing at the Sangam is believed to cleanse sins. The Kumbh Mela is recognised by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March; the annual Magh Mela is held in January–February.
destinations.guidelines: Agree boat fares in advance and use life jackets where provided.

destinations.name: Allahabad Fort
destinations.summary: Akbar's massive fort at the confluence, home to the revered Akshayavat tree and Patalpuri temple.
destinations.summaryHi: संगम पर अकबर का विशाल किला, जहाँ पवित्र अक्षयवट और पातालपुरी मंदिर हैं।
destinations.description: The fort stands on the banks of the Yamuna near the Sangam. Much of it is used by the Indian Army, and public access is limited to specific areas such as the Patalpuri temple and the Akshayavat.
destinations.history: Emperor Akbar built the fort in 1583. It later came under British control and contains an Ashokan pillar inscribed with edicts from the 3rd century BCE.
destinations.culturalSignificance: The Akshayavat ('indestructible banyan') is mentioned in Hindu traditions and is an important stop for pilgrims to the Sangam.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March.
destinations.guidelines: Access is restricted because of army use — confirm which areas are open locally before visiting.

destinations.name: Anand Bhavan
destinations.summary: The Nehru family home, now a museum about India's freedom struggle.
destinations.summaryHi: नेहरू परिवार का निवास, जो अब स्वतंत्रता संग्राम से जुड़ा संग्रहालय है।
destinations.description: A historic mansion preserved with original furnishings, photographs and documents of the Nehru family and the independence movement; the adjacent Swaraj Bhavan and a planetarium are nearby.
destinations.history: Motilal Nehru bought the property in the late 19th century. It became a centre of the independence movement, hosting leaders of the Indian National Congress. Indira Gandhi donated Anand Bhavan to the nation in 1970.
destinations.culturalSignificance: A key site for understanding the political history of modern India.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March. Museums often close one day a week — check before you go.

destinations.name: Shri Krishna Janmasthan
destinations.summary: The temple complex around the site revered as the birthplace of Lord Krishna.
destinations.summaryHi: भगवान कृष्ण के जन्मस्थान माने जाने वाले स्थल पर बना मंदिर परिसर।
destinations.description: The complex includes the Garbha Griha shrine marking the traditional birthplace, the Keshavdeva temple and the Bhagavata Bhavan.
destinations.history: Temples have been built and destroyed at this site several times over the centuries. The present complex was developed in the 20th century.
destinations.culturalSignificance: Mathura is one of Hinduism's seven sacred cities. Janmashtami, Krishna's birth festival, draws enormous crowds.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March; Janmashtami (August/September) and Holi are spectacular but extremely crowded.
destinations.guidelines: High security with restrictions on items allowed inside — check current rules. Dress modestly.

destinations.name: Banke Bihari Temple
destinations.summary: Vrindavan's most beloved Krishna temple, known for its joyous, crowded darshan.
destinations.summaryHi: वृंदावन का सबसे प्रिय कृष्ण मंदिर, जहाँ दर्शन बेहद उल्लासपूर्ण होते हैं।
destinations.description: The temple houses the image of Banke Bihari (Krishna in a 'thrice-bent' pose). A curtain is drawn in front of the deity at short intervals during darshan, a unique local custom.
destinations.history: The deity is associated with the 16th-century saint-musician Swami Haridas; the present temple building dates from the 1860s.
destinations.culturalSignificance: Central to Vrindavan's devotional life, especially during Holi and Janmashtami.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March; weekdays are less crowded.
destinations.guidelines: Extremely crowded at peak times — avoid carrying valuables and take care of children and elderly companions.

destinations.name: Prem Mandir
destinations.summary: A modern white-marble temple to Radha-Krishna and Sita-Ram, famous for its evening illumination.
destinations.summaryHi: राधा-कृष्ण और सीता-राम को समर्पित आधुनिक सफ़ेद संगमरमर मंदिर, शाम की रोशनी के लिए प्रसिद्ध।
destinations.description: The temple's carved marble walls depict episodes from Krishna's life; landscaped grounds hold tableaux and a musical fountain.
destinations.history: Prem Mandir was established by Jagadguru Kripalu Parishat, founded by Jagadguru Shri Kripalu Ji Maharaj, and was inaugurated in 2012.
destinations.culturalSignificance: A major new landmark of Vrindavan that attracts pilgrims and tourists in large numbers.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: Evenings for the lighting; October to March.

destinations.name: Dudhwa National Park
destinations.summary: Terai grasslands and sal forests near the Nepal border, home to tigers, swamp deer and one-horned rhinos.
destinations.summaryHi: नेपाल सीमा के पास तराई घास के मैदान और साल वन — बाघ, बारहसिंगा और गैंडों का घर।
destinations.description: Dudhwa protects one of the last stretches of Terai ecosystem in India. Safaris pass through tall grasslands, wetlands and sal forest rich in birdlife.
destinations.history: Dudhwa was declared a national park in 1977 and became part of the Dudhwa Tiger Reserve in 1987. Greater one-horned rhinoceroses were reintroduced here in 1984.
destinations.culturalSignificance: A conservation success story associated with naturalist Billy Arjan Singh, who campaigned for its protection.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: November to March for pleasant weather. The park is typically closed during the monsoon — confirm season dates with the UP Forest Department.
destinations.guidelines: Safaris must be booked through authorised channels. Follow forest rules: no littering, no loud noise, stay inside vehicles.

destinations.name: Jhansi Fort
destinations.summary: A hilltop Bundela fort forever linked with Rani Lakshmibai and the 1857 uprising.
destinations.summaryHi: पहाड़ी पर बना बुंदेला किला, जो रानी लक्ष्मीबाई और 1857 के संग्राम से जुड़ा है।
destinations.description: The granite fort crowns a rocky hill in Jhansi, with ramparts, temples and viewpoints over the city; the Rani Mahal and a government museum are nearby.
destinations.history: Raja Bir Singh Deo of Orchha built the fort in 1613. In 1857–58 Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi defended it against British forces before her legendary escape and death in battle.
destinations.culturalSignificance: Rani Lakshmibai is one of India's most celebrated freedom fighters, and the fort is a pilgrimage site for history lovers.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March.

destinations.name: Chunar Fort
destinations.summary: A sandstone fort on a rocky outcrop above the Ganga, about 40 km from Varanasi.
destinations.summaryHi: वाराणसी से लगभग 40 किमी दूर गंगा के ऊपर चट्टान पर बना बलुआ पत्थर का किला।
destinations.description: Chunar Fort offers sweeping views of a bend in the Ganga and contains old wells, gateways and a sun dial; Chunar is also known for its sandstone and pottery.
destinations.history: The fort's strategic position made it contested by successive powers, including Sher Shah Suri, the Mughals under Humayun and Akbar, and later the British East India Company. Local legends link its origins to King Vikramaditya.
destinations.culturalSignificance: Celebrated in Hindi literature, notably in Devaki Nandan Khatri's fantasy novel Chandrakanta.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March; works well as a day trip from Varanasi.

destinations.name: Mahaparinirvana Temple, Kushinagar
destinations.summary: Where the Buddha attained parinirvana — a peaceful shrine with a great reclining Buddha statue.
destinations.summaryHi: जहाँ बुद्ध ने महापरिनिर्वाण प्राप्त किया — विशाल लेटी हुई बुद्ध प्रतिमा वाला शांत मंदिर।
destinations.description: The temple houses a large reclining statue of the Buddha; behind it stands the Nirvana Stupa. Nearby are the Ramabhar Stupa (cremation site) and temples built by Buddhist nations.
destinations.history: Kushinagar is where the Buddha passed away and attained final nirvana. The site was rediscovered in the 19th century, and the reclining statue was excavated in 1876 during archaeological work led by A. C. L. Carlleyle.
destinations.culturalSignificance: One of the four principal Buddhist pilgrimage sites, visited by pilgrims from across Asia.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March. Buddha Purnima is an especially significant time.
destinations.guidelines: Maintain silence inside the shrine. Remove footwear where requested.

destinations.name: Gorakhnath Math
destinations.summary: The principal temple and monastery of the Nath tradition, named after Guru Gorakhnath.
destinations.summaryHi: नाथ परंपरा का प्रमुख मंदिर और मठ, गुरु गोरखनाथ के नाम पर।
destinations.description: A large temple complex with landscaped grounds and a lake, at the centre of Gorakhpur's religious life.
destinations.history: The math is the seat of the Nath sampradaya of yogis tracing their lineage to the medieval yogi Gorakhnath, after whom the city of Gorakhpur is named.
destinations.culturalSignificance: The Khichdi Mela held around Makar Sankranti draws large numbers of devotees offering khichdi at the temple.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March; Makar Sankranti in mid-January for the Khichdi Mela.
